name: cutscene-mcp

tools.name: search_library
tools.description: Find pieces of the library by meaning, in French or English: shots, transitions, effects, animations, camera moves, 3-D objects, sounds, music, looks and montages (whole films ready to fill). An empty query lists a kind (`total` says how many there are; `offset` gives the next page). Returns ids to use with the other tools.

query.description: What is wanted, in plain words: "a phone showing the app", "soft transition", "keyboard sound", "retro"…

kinds.description: Keep to these kinds of pieces

offset.description: Skip this many results: the next page of a long list

lang.description: Language of the names in the answer (default en)

tools.name: get_piece
tools.description: Everything about one piece: what it is for, how long it may last, its settings and their choices, and for a shot its elements (texts, 3-D objects) and every word it shows as an example (`words`, by the key set_text takes; `settings` says which words take *asterisks* and which settings only show once written). Read it before filling a shot.

lang.description: Language of the names and of the example words (default en)

tools.name: list_montages
tools.description: The films that are already cut (launch, feature drop, demo, teaser…): their shots in order and their length, the templates of the working folder included (one's own, and those taken from what people shared). Start a film from one with create_film, then change what needs changing.

tools.name: list_films
tools.description: The films kept in the working folder, most recent first.

tools.name: create_film
tools.description: Start a film: from a montage (recommended: it comes cut, with transitions, music and sounds) or empty. Give the brand here or later with set_brand. The film is a .cutscene.json file in the working folder; the same file opens in the Cutscene editor.

name.description: A short name for the file, e.g. launch-acme

montage.description: A montage id (see list_montages). Without one the film is empty

title.description: The film's title (default: the product's name, else the file's name)

format.description: 16:9 (default), 9:16, 4:5 or 1:1. Can change later: shots recompose themselves

lang.description: Language of the example words (default en)

product.description: The product's name and tagline, used by the montage where it shows them

overwrite.description: Replace a film that already has this name (undo_film puts it back)

colors.description: bg = background, surface = cards, ink = text, muted = quiet text, accent = the brand's colour (key words, buttons), accent2 = a second colour (a word that turns on a ground of the brand's colour, a second dot). Left out, accent2 is a deep shade of accent

fonts.description: Font families of the library (see the guide resource for the list)

radius.description: Corner radius of cards and screens: 4 sharp, 16 soft, 28 round

logo.description: Path of a logo file on this machine (SVG or PNG on a transparent ground; the empty room around the mark is cut off), or null for none

tools.name: get_film
tools.description: A film in a few lines: its shots in order with their words (a leading * marks an example nobody wrote yet; `examples` lists the same keys), transitions, music, the sounds placed by hand and how many the shots bring. With sounds: true, every sound the shots and transitions bring, with its moment and the id set_sound takes. With full: true, the whole document.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

sounds.description: true lists every sound the shots and transitions bring (often several dozen)

full.description: true for the whole document instead of the short form

tools.name: edit_film
tools.description: Apply changes to a film, in order and all together (if one is refused nothing is written, and the answer says which and why). Shots are named by position (1 = first). Typical: set_text to write the words, set_shot to fill lists and pictures, set_transition (and set_settings for its direction or strength), set_music, add_shot / replace_shot / duplicate_shot / remove_shot, fit_film to reach a length in seconds, use_template to start again from another montage. undo_film puts back the film as it was before the call.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

at.description: Position the new shot takes (1 = first). Default: at the end

beats.description: Length in beats of the music. Left out: the piece's usual length

seconds.description: Its length in seconds, instead of beats

content.description: Settings of the shot by key (see get_piece): a text, a list of lines, a choice, true/false, a picture's file path. null puts the example back.

shot.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

piece.description: The shot piece that takes its place; words and pictures that still apply are kept

shot.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id
A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id
A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

at.description: Position the copy takes (1 = first). Default: right after the shot

shot.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

beats.description: Length in beats of the music, by quarters of a beat (seconds = beats × 60 / the film's bpm). Brought back into what the piece allows, and the answer says so

seconds.description: Its length in seconds, instead of beats: brought back into what the piece allows, and the answer says so

content.description: Settings of the shot by key (see get_piece): a text, a list of lines, a choice, true/false, a picture's file path. null puts the example back.

colors.description: Draw this shot alone in other colours than the brand's (a dark shot in a light film): its ground, its words and its drawings follow together. Give bg and ink together so the words still read. null gives the whole shot back to the brand

anyOf.description: Some of the brand's colours, given again for this one alone: bg = its ground, surface = a card's or a screen's fill, ink = its words, muted = its quiet words, accent = its key parts (a button, a mark, key words), accent2 = a second colour. Only those given change; null gives one back to the brand

camera.description: A camera piece (camera/push…), or null for the shot's own

sounds.description: false silences the sounds the shot brings

shot.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

layer.description: Key of a text of the shot (see get_film: texts)

text.description: The words. *Asterisks* put words in the brand's accent colour. Empty puts the example back

shot.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

layer.description: Key of an element of the shot (a text, a 3-D object, bg for the background). "texts" stands for every text of the shot at once (their animation, effects, colour, type, opacity: not their place)

animation.description: text-anim/… for a text, anim/… for anything else; null puts the shot's own back

delay_beats.description: Entrance moved later (or earlier) by this many beats

delay_seconds.description: The same in seconds, instead of beats: 0.5 = half a second later, -0.5 sooner, 0 = when the shot brings it

place.description: Move or resize the element, in the film's current format only (each format lays itself out its own way). What is left out stays as it is. null puts it back where the shot places it, at its own size. Check the result with preview_film

at.description: Where it goes in the picture, inside the margins. center, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right place it both ways; top, bottom, left, right move it along that side only

x.description: Where its centre goes, in fractions of the frame from its left edge (0.5 = the middle). See get_film: where

y.description: Where its centre goes, in fractions of the frame from its top

dx.description: Or: how far from where the shot places it, in fractions of the frame's width (0.1 = a tenth to the right)

dy.description: The same downwards, in fractions of the frame's height

scale.description: Its size, 1 being the size the shot gives it (2 = twice as large). A text is set again at that size

rotate.description: Turn it flat on the screen, like a sheet turned on a table, in degrees clockwise from how the shot draws it. This is what « tourne », « penche », « incline », « de travers », "tilt it a bit" ask for: 4 to 8 is a little, -8 leans it to the left. 0 puts it straight again. In every format

tilt.description: Lean it in depth, in degrees, like a card turned in space: « en perspective », « de trois quarts », « vu de côté » (a 3-D object turns on itself). Not for something leaned a little on the screen: that is rotate. null: flat again

x.description: Leans its top away from the viewer (negative: its bottom)

y.description: Turns its right edge away from the viewer (negative: its left edge)

scale.description: Its size, said here instead of in place: the same as place.scale

opacity.description: How much of it shows: 1 as the shot draws it, 0.5 half see-through

color.description: A text: the colour of its letters. Any other element: its key colour (what the brand's accent is for it). null: the brand's again

colors.description: Draw this element alone in other colours than the brand's. null gives it back to the brand

anyOf.description: Some of the brand's colours, given again for this one alone: bg = its ground, surface = a card's or a screen's fill, ink = its words, muted = its quiet words, accent = its key parts (a button, a mark, key words), accent2 = a second colour. Only those given change; null gives one back to the brand

type.description: A text's own type: only what is given changes; null for one of them, or for all, gives it back to the shot. Its size is place.scale

font.description: A font family of the library

weight.description: 300 light, 400 regular, 600 semi-bold, 700 bold (« gras »), 800 to 900 heavy (« bien gras », « très gras »)

align.description: How its lines sit in its box

order.description: front draws it over the other elements of its shot, back under them. null: where the shot draws it

after.description: Position of the shot before the join (1 = between shots 1 and 2), or "all" for every join of the film

piece.description: A transition piece; transition/cut for a plain cut. With after "all", a list of pieces is dealt along the film, one per join in turn (« une transition différente à chaque fois »). Left out: the one in place keeps its place and only its length, its settings or what travels change

beats.description: Length in beats (halves count). Left out: the transition's usual length, or the one in place

seconds.description: Its length in seconds, instead of beats

carry.description: Key of an element both shots share, which then travels from one to the other

settings.description: Settings of a transition, an effect, an animation or a camera move, by key (see get_piece): each takes one of the values listed there

piece.description: A piece already in the film that has settings: a transition, an effect, an animation (anim/…), a camera move

after.description: For a transition: the shot before the join. May be left out when the film uses this transition once

shot.description: For a camera move, an animation or an effect on an element: its shot. An effect over the whole picture takes neither shot nor layer

layer.description: For an animation or an effect on an element: the element's key

settings.description: Settings of a transition, an effect, an animation or a camera move, by key (see get_piece): each takes one of the values listed there

shot.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

beat.description: Beats after the start of that shot. Left out with `second` and `on`: on the shot's first frame

second.description: Seconds after the start of that shot, instead of beats

on.description: Key of an element of that shot: the sound falls as that element comes in (its entrance as it is now). Instead of beat or second

gain_db.description: Its level: 0 as it comes, -6 clearly quieter, +3 a little louder

pan.description: -1 in the left ear, 1 in the right, 0 in the middle

id.description: Id of a sound placed with add_sound (see get_film: sounds.placed). A sound piece (sfx/key) takes away every sound of that kind: those placed are removed, those the shots bring are silenced

Id of a sound of the film (see get_film: sounds.placed, and sounds.brought for those the shots and transitions bring). Or a sound piece (sfx/key): every sound of that kind in the film at once (« les bruits de clavier »), with muted or a level

shot.description: A placed sound: the shot it now belongs to

beat.description: A placed sound: beats after the start of its shot

second.description: A placed sound: seconds after the start of its shot, instead of beats

on.description: A placed sound: key of an element of its shot, as the sound should fall when that element comes in

pan.description: A placed sound: -1 in the left ear, 1 in the right, 0 in the middle

muted.description: A sound a shot or a transition brings: true silences this one, false brings it back. With a sound piece as id: all of that kind

piece.description: A music piece (the film takes its tempo, and every shot keeps its length in seconds), or null for no music. Left out: the music in place stays

gain_db.description: Its level: 0 as it comes, -3 a little quieter, -6 clearly quieter, +3 a little louder

full_from.description: The shot on which the music comes in full (its rhythm and its bass): held back before it, and down again under the last shot. null: decided from what the shots show

anyOf.description: A shot: its position in the film (1 = first) or its id

montage.description: A montage piece (see list_montages): its shots, transitions, music and sounds replace the film's. The brand, the title, the format and the language stay

seconds.description: The length the whole film should have: every shot gets shorter or longer in proportion, within what it allows. A length the shots cannot reach is not reached, and the answer says how far it went

drop.description: true: when its shots cannot make the film that short, take out as few of them as it takes, from the middle (never the first nor the last, those nobody filled in first). The answer says which. Left out: no shot is removed

colors.description: bg = background, surface = cards, ink = text, muted = quiet text, accent = the brand's main colour (key words, buttons), accent2 = a second colour. Only those given change. The text must read on the background: change ink, muted and surface together with bg

fonts.description: Font families of the library: display = headlines, text = running text, mono = small labels

radius.description: Corner radius of cards and screens: 4 sharp, 16 soft, 28 round

logo.description: A logo picture the person gave (its file path, or the name of the file they handed over). null takes the logo off: the shots that show it show the name

format.description: 16:9 = horizontal (landscape), 9:16 = vertical (tall), 1:1 = square, 4:5 = portrait. Every shot recomposes itself for the format

look.description: A style (look/night, look/glass…): its grounds, its type and its finish for the whole film. A colour the brand was given stays the film's main colour; a film with nobody's colour takes the style's own

effects.description: Effects over the whole picture (effect/grain…), replacing the current ones

sounds.description: false silences every sound the shots and transitions bring (the music and the sounds placed by hand stay); true brings them back

changes.description: The changes, applied in order: 1 to 40 of them

tools.name: set_brand
tools.description: The name, colours, fonts, corner radius and logo of the whole film. Only what is given changes. Make sure the text colour reads on the background (check_film measures it).

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

colors.description: bg = background, surface = cards, ink = text, muted = quiet text, accent = the brand's colour (key words, buttons), accent2 = a second colour (a word that turns on a ground of the brand's colour, a second dot). Left out, accent2 is a deep shade of accent

fonts.description: Font families of the library (see the guide resource for the list)

radius.description: Corner radius of cards and screens: 4 sharp, 16 soft, 28 round

logo.description: Path of a logo file on this machine (SVG or PNG on a transparent ground; the empty room around the mark is cut off), or null for none

tools.name: check_film
tools.description: Everything that stands between the film and a good export, in one answer: example words and lists nobody rewrote (by shot, with the keys set_text and set_shot take), pictures not given yet or that cannot be drawn, the brand's name and logo, text contrast (WCAG, 4.5), long texts, lines the film does not leave the time to read, shots too short for what they hold, the film's and each shot's length in seconds, music and sounds, premium pieces, and what the plan exports. It ends with `next`: what to do, in order. Run it before export_film and before telling the user the film is done.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

formats.description: The formats meant for export (default: the film's own): the plan is checked for each

uhd.description: true checks the plan for a 4K export

tools.name: preview_film
tools.description: A contact sheet of the film as a picture: one frame per shot by default (taken once its elements have arrived), three frames of one shot, 2 to 8 instants spread across one shot (frames, to judge its motion), chosen moments, or a transition from its last frame before to its first frame after (join; eight frames, frames gives 4 to 12). Look at it after each round of changes: it is the only way to see the result. What the plan adds to an export (the free plan's end mark, bottom right over the last two seconds) is drawn here too. For one frame at full size, use still_film.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

shots.description: Only these shots (one shot alone is shown arriving, settled and leaving)

frames.description: With one shot in shots: this many instants (2 to 8) spread from its first to its last moment, to judge how it moves. With join: how many frames of the transition (4 to 12)

join.description: The transition after this shot, frame by frame

format.description: Look at another format than the film's own

tools.name: still_film
tools.description: ONE frame of the film at full size (1920×1080 in 16:9), to read small text or check a detail a contact sheet is too small for. Give a time in seconds (at) or a shot number (taken once its elements have arrived); without either, the first shot.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

at.description: A time in seconds from the start of the film

shot.description: A shot (1 = first), shown once its elements have arrived

format.description: Look at another format than the film's own

png.description: true for a PNG without loss (heavier). Default: JPEG

tools.name: export_film
tools.description: Render the film to MP4 files (H.264, 60 fps, sound mixed and mastered) in the working folder's exports/, one per format. Each file is checked for dangerous flashes. The plan decides which formats and definitions are open; premium pieces need a paid plan. A long job: progress is reported to a client that asks for it, and a cancelled request stops the render. Run check_film first.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

tools.name: export_still
tools.description: Write ONE frame of the film as a picture file in the working folder's exports/ (PNG, or JPEG): a poster for a thumbnail, a social card, a web page. Give a time in seconds (at) or a shot number (taken once its elements have arrived); without either, the first shot. Look at the frame with still_film first. The plan gates it like export_film (premium pieces, formats).

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

at.description: A time in seconds from the start of the film

shot.description: A shot (1 = first), taken once its elements have arrived

tools.name: undo_film
tools.description: Put a film back as it was before its last change (edit_film, set_brand, a restore, an overwrite). The version it replaces is kept, so calling it again puts that one back: two undos cancel out. To go further back, use list_versions and restore_version.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: The earlier versions of a film, most recent first: every change keeps the film it replaced (the 20 most recent). Each has an id to give to restore_version, the moment it was written, and its length and number of shots.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Put an earlier version of a film back (an id from list_versions). The film it replaces is kept as a version too, so undo_film cancels the restore.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

version.description: A version id from list_versions, e.g. 2026-10-06T21-42-21-123Z

tools.name: duplicate_film
tools.description: A copy of a film under another name, to try a variant (another montage order, another look, another language) without touching the original.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

title.description: A title for the copy (default: the same)

tools.name: rename_film
tools.description: Give a film another name in the working folder. Its earlier versions follow it; files already exported keep their names. The title shown inside the film only changes when title is given.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

tools.name: delete_film
tools.description: Take a film out of the working folder. It needs confirm: true, and the user's word first. The file is moved to the folder's .trash/ with its earlier versions, not erased: the answer says where, and moving it back puts the film back. Exported files stay.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

confirm.description: Must be true: say so only once the user agreed

tools.name: piece_example
tools.description: How to write a piece of your own for the library, with a model that passes: a template (montage), a style (look), a shot composed of elements, a transition or an effect (a fragment shader), an element animation, a text animation, a camera move. A piece is data (a recipe), never code that runs, except the shader of a transition or an effect. Read the model, change it, then create_piece.

kind.description: The kind of piece to write

annotations.title: A model to write a piece from

tools.name: create_piece
tools.description: Write a piece of your own into the working folder (pieces/): a recipe of the shape piece_example shows. It is read first (its shape, its shader's words, the pieces it names) and refused with what is wrong; check_piece then compiles and draws it. Once written it is used like any piece of the library, by its id, in this folder's films: add_shot, set_transition, set_element… and search_library finds it. A film that uses it carries its recipe, so the film file stays whole; rewriting a piece (overwrite: true) updates the films of the folder that use it. Every word a shot shows must be an example the user will rewrite: a recipe never claims anything.

recipe.description: The recipe (see piece_example). Its id may be left out (it is given one from its kind and its name) or chosen: <kind>/c- then 4 to 24 lower-case letters or figures, e.g. transition/c-diagonalwipe

overwrite.description: Rewrite the piece that has this id

annotations.title: Write a piece of your own

tools.name: list_my_pieces
tools.description: The pieces written in the working folder (pieces/), most recent first. To take one out, delete_piece; films that already use it keep working, they carry its recipe.

tools.name: check_piece
tools.description: Pass a piece of the working folder through the gates every piece of the library passes, drawn by the real engine: its shader compiles and is not heavy, it meets a dozen shots of every family wide and tall without an error, a bare ground or a jump, it never flashes between a dark shot and a light one; a shot holds awkward content in the four formats, opens on something and never stands still; a template builds whole. Answers what is wrong in sentences, with a picture of the piece at work. Takes a few seconds to a minute.

id.description: The id of a piece of the working folder (see list_my_pieces)

annotations.title: Check a piece of your own

tools.name: search_community
tools.description: The pieces other people shared and a person approved (templates, styles, shots, transitions, effects, animations, camera moves), most used first: who made each, how many films kept it, its rating once enough people rated it. Reached through the user's account at the app. To use one, use_community_piece { id }.

query.description: Words to look for in the names, the descriptions and the tags, in French or English. Left out: everything

kind.description: Keep to one kind of piece

lang.description: Language of the names in the answer (default en)

tools.name: use_community_piece
tools.description: Bring a piece somebody shared into the working folder (pieces/), with the pieces it needs: it is then used by its id like any piece of the library (add_shot, set_transition, create_film with a shared template…), and a film that uses it carries its recipe. A piece is data that was read and drawn before a person approved it, never code that runs.

id.description: The id of a shared piece (see search_community), e.g. transition/c-k3m9x2p7q4wd

annotations.title: Take a shared piece into the folder

tools.name: film_as_piece
tools.description: Make a piece of the working folder out of a film, so it can be used again or shared. As a template: its shots in order with their lengths and choices, its transitions, its music and its finishing; the pictures, the logo, the brand's name and its colours do not leave, and with words: false neither do the texts its author wrote (the library's examples take their place). As a style: its colours, its fonts, its corners and its finishing, never its name or its logo. The piece is then like any other of the folder: start a film from it (create_film { montage }) or dress one in it (edit_film: set_film { look }), check_piece it, and publish_piece it once the user agrees. A template that follows another one too closely is refused when it is shared: the answer says how close this one is.

name.description: The film's name in the working folder (see list_films)

as.description: template: the whole film as a film to start from. style: its colours and type alone

title.description: The piece's name, in French and in English (not the product's name: others will use it for theirs)

about.description: One sentence on what it is for, in both languages

words.description: A template only. false keeps the author's own texts out: the library's examples stand in their place. Default true: they stay as example words

annotations.title: Turn a film into a template or a style

tools.name: publish_piece
tools.description: Share a piece of the working folder with everybody who uses Cutscene. It is first passed through the gates here (check_piece: a piece that fails is not sent), then kept on the user's account and sent to the person of the Cutscene team who checks what is shared; nothing is visible to others before that person accepts it (their answer comes within 3 days at most), and the user can take it back from their account page (« Mes partages »). A template may start from another one, not copy it: one whose cut is more than two thirds the same as a template already in the library is refused, and the refusal names that template. What leaves is the piece alone (its recipe, with its example words): never a film, its words, its logo or its pictures. It needs the app's address and a key of the user's account (CUTSCENE_APP_URL, CUTSCENE_TOKEN), confirm: true, and the user's word first: their piece leaves their machine, under the name they choose to show (public_name) or none. Sharing is a permission its author gives, each time: before confirm: true, put it to the user in their own language and get their yes. The permission: “By sharing, you allow Cutscene, free of charge, to show this piece in its library, and its users to use it and change it in their films, commercial and advertising ones included, without having to credit you (Terms, article 12). If you remove the share, the films already made with it keep it. Sharing is for adults only.” Sharing the same piece again sends a new version, and needs their yes again.

id.description: The id of a piece of the working folder (see list_my_pieces)

public_name.description: The name shown next to the piece as its author. Left out: the one the account already shows, or none

confirm.description: Must be true: say so only once the user read the permission and agreed to share this piece

annotations.title: Share a piece of your own with others

tools.name: delete_piece
tools.description: Take a piece out of the working folder. It needs confirm: true, and the user's word first. The file is moved to .trash/, not erased. Films that already use the piece keep working: they carry its recipe.

id.description: The id of a piece of the working folder

confirm.description: Must be true: say so only once the user agreed

annotations.title: Delete a piece of your own

instructions:
# Making a film with Cutscene

Cutscene assembles motion-design films (product launches, feature drops, demos, teasers) from a library of 416 ready-made pieces. You place pieces and fill them; you never draw or animate by hand. Films are files (name.cutscene.json) in the working folder; the same file opens in the Cutscene editor. Every change keeps the film it replaced (the last 20): undo_film, list_versions, restore_version.

## The method
1. Know the product first: what it does, for whom, the one thing to remember, the call to action; screenshots and logo as file paths; brand colours. Ask for what is missing.
2. list_montages, then create_film from the montage that fits (27 of them, from 6 to 61 s), with the brand. A montage comes cut: shots, transitions, music, sounds on the beat.
3. get_film. Texts that start with * are examples nobody wrote yet (each shot lists their keys in `examples`). Write them with edit_film set_text, including the words drawn inside an element (a button's label, a figure, a price). Fill lists and pictures with set_shot { content }. get_piece tells what a shot takes.
4. preview_film and LOOK at the picture, after every round of changes. One shot's motion: preview_film { shots: [n], frames: 6 }. A transition, frame by frame: preview_film { join: n }. Small text: still_film.
5. check_film: what is still an example, pictures missing or that cannot be drawn, name and logo, contrast, lines the film leaves no time to read, shots too short for what they hold, what the plan exports, and `next`, what to do in order. Never call a film done before it is clean and looked at.
6. export_film (export_still for a poster). Tell the user where the files are and what is still theirs.

## A good launch film (15 to 45 s)
- The hook: the problem or the result. A template's « Meet X. » is an example: rewrite it.
- The product: its name and what it does, in one line.
- Two or three gestures: the product at work (devices and 3-d objects, interface in use, features), one per shot, on the user's own screenshots.
- Proof only if the user gave one (a figure, a quote, a customer). Without one, remove that shot.
- The call: one action, with the name or the logo. Then stop.
A feature drop is one gesture between a hook and a call (about 15 s). A teaser is a hook and a call (under 10 s).

## Words
- One idea per shot. A headline is 2 to 6 words; the line under it stays short. A title keeps the line breaks you write (\n); a line too wide for its box wraps, then the type shrinks: shorter lines give larger type.
- Put one or two key words between *asterisks*: a text takes them in the brand's accent colour (never the whole line). Words a drawing writes itself (a button, a caption in a pill, a figure) are one colour: the asterisks are left out. get_piece says which is which.
- Use the user's words, figures and screenshots. Never invent a customer, a quote, a logo, an award, a price or a number: leave the example or remove the shot, and say what is missing.

## Time
Give lengths in seconds (`seconds`, `delay_seconds`, `second`). A piece's range holds in seconds (see get_piece); under another music every shot keeps the seconds it had. Leave time to read, a third of a second a word once the words are there: a transition covers the end of the shot it leaves and the start of the next, so count outside it (check_film lists the lines short of time).

## Which piece when
montage (27), shot (128), transition (68), effect (18), text-anim (27), anim (15), camera (16), model (9), sfx (76), music (24), look (8). search_library finds them in French or English.
- montage: where a film starts. shot: one idea; replace_shot keeps the words that still apply.
- transition: a plain cut is fine; few kinds per film. Families: cut (cuts, 9), camera (zooms and camera, 15), morph (morphs, 9), matte (track mattes, 16), space (in 3-d, 7), soft (dissolves and slides, 12). Zooms, match cuts, morphs and track mattes carry a film. Between two shots that each show a clear subject, match-subject keeps the eye on it, zoom-into goes into it, pull-out comes out of it, shape-morph turns one into the other. set_transition { carry: key } makes a shared element travel.
- text-anim, anim, camera: only to change how a shot already moves. effect: one or two, on an element or on the whole picture.
- look: a style (grounds, type, finish) in one move; the brand's own colour stays. music: one per film. sfx: add_sound on a moment that should be felt; shots bring their own.

## Changes (edit_film)
One call takes up to 40 changes, applied together or not at all.
- Shots: add_shot, replace_shot, duplicate_shot, move_shot, remove_shot; set_shot (length, lists, pictures, camera, its sounds, `colors` of its own). use_template starts again from another montage; fit_film { seconds } brings the whole film to a length.
- Words: set_text. Elements, with set_element: hide, animate, effects, and by hand `place` (at: "top-right"…, or x and y; scale sizes it, a text too), `rotate`, `tilt` (in depth), `opacity`, `color` or `colors` (for it alone), `type` (one text's font, weight, italics, capitals, alignment), `order` (front, back). get_film says where each element is (`where`) and when it comes in (`arrives`).
- Joins: set_transition (after: a position or "all"); set_settings changes what is already placed (a push's direction, a glow's strength).
- Sound: set_music (`full_from`: the shot it comes in full on), add_sound (`on`: as an element comes in), set_sound, remove_sound; set_film { sounds: false } silences what the shots bring. You cannot hear: keep the shots' sounds, choose the music by its mood.
- Whole film: set_film (title, format, language, look, effects), set_brand. film_as_piece makes a template or a style out of a film.
An unknown argument or setting is refused by name, never dropped.

## A piece of your own
When nothing in the library does what is needed, write a piece: piece_example { kind } gives a model and its rules (a template, a style, a shot, a transition or an effect as a shader, an animation, a camera move), create_piece writes it into the folder, then used by its id like any other. check_piece compiles it, draws it and passes it through the library's own gates. Rewriting a piece (overwrite: true) updates the films that use it. A piece is data, never code that runs; every word a shot shows stays an example the user rewrites.
Other people share pieces: search_community lists them, use_community_piece brings one into the folder. publish_piece shares one of the user's own, only on their word, with their account's key (CUTSCENE_TOKEN, CUTSCENE_APP_URL); a person checks it first, within 3 days; template copies are refused.

## Formats and the plan
16:9 for X, YouTube and websites; 9:16 for Reels, TikTok, Shorts; 4:5 for Instagram and LinkedIn; 1:1 everywhere. Shots recompose themselves, nothing is cropped: check each format with preview_film { format }. Words are shared by every format; set_element { place } holds in the current format only: look at a film in each format it is meant for.
Without a paid plan, exports are 16:9, 9:16 at 1080p with a small end mark (previews show it), from base pieces. Premium pieces can be placed and previewed; exporting them, the other formats and 4K need a paid plan. check_film says what the plan exports: tell the user before building in a format it does not.

## The words the user reads
Speak to the user with the editor's words, not the tool names: a montage is a "template" (« modèle »), a look a "style" (« style »), sfx "sound effects" (« bruitages »), a join a "transition", a premium piece a "Pro piece" (« pièce Pro »). Give lengths in seconds, never in beats or BPM.

## Fonts for set_brand
Titles: Funnel Display, Bricolage Grotesque, Space Grotesk, Unbounded, Anton, Bebas Neue, Archivo Black, Instrument Serif, Fraunces, Newsreader, or any text font. Text: Funnel Sans, Geist, Inter, DM Sans, Manrope, Plus Jakarta Sans, Figtree, Hanken Grotesk, Instrument Sans, Schibsted Grotesk. Figures and code: Geist Mono, JetBrains Mono.

## Pictures
A picture (a shot's screen, the logo in set_brand) is the path of a file on this machine, PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG or GIF: set_shot { content: { screen: "/path/to/capture.png" } }. The empty room around a logo is cut off. A capture taller than wide goes in a phone, under a fingertip; a wide one in a window, under a pointer. To aim a click, a zoom or a spotlight at a place of the capture: set_shot { content: { spotX: 82, spotY: 18 } }, hundredths from its left and from its top; `spot` chooses among five places instead. A picture made elsewhere is a file too: give its path.
